title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Aisha Patel
description: Background: CI and canary telemetry indicated intermittent starvation for low-token, latency-sensitive requests when the continuous-batcher consolidated long-running, high-token requests. Motivation: reduce tail latency variability and prevent request starvation while preserving batching efficiency. This PR introduces a set of scheduler and queueing changes to the continuous-batcher runtime: 1) priority-aware queueing with per-priority token buckets and weight-based dequeueing to ensure small/low-latency requests make progress alongside large requests; 2) request aging (queue-time tracking) with an aging boost that temporarily raises scheduling weight for requests that reach configured thresholds; 3) adaptive per-request max-wait-timeouts (configurable default: 150ms for low-latency class, 500ms for standard) to bound head-of-line blocking and trigger graceful fallback/fast-path execution; 4) backpressure signals to upstream routing (via existing request metadata) when queue depth exceeds soft and hard thresholds; 5) metrics, tracing hooks, and internal perf counters to observe queue length by priority, starvation incidents, timeout triggers, and reclaimed batches; 6) microbench harness for targeted scheduler latencies and end-to-end canary scenario used during rollout. Implementation notes: - scheduler/sweep loop refactored to compute effective weights once per cycle and to prefer ready requests with wait_time >= aging_threshold. - token bucket used to limit serialized token allocation per-priority and avoid single large request monopolizing GPU kernel submission. - added metrics: continuous_batcher.queue_length_by_priority, continuous_batcher.starvation_incidents, continuous_batcher.request_aging_boosts, continuous_batcher.timeout_trigger_count. - new config knobs (runtime config / env override): cb.scheduler.aging_threshold_ms, cb.scheduler.max_wait_low_latency_ms, cb.scheduler.max_wait_standard_ms, cb.scheduler.soft_queue_limit, cb.scheduler.hard_queue_limit. - added unit tests for weight computation and aging boost, and an integration test that simulates mixed small/large workloads. Checklist: - [x] scheduler algorithm changes implemented - [x] unit tests added - [x] integration/canary harness added - [x] metrics + tracing hooks added - [x] docs/CHANGELOG entry - [x] perf microbench results attached The description below includes rationale for key choices: *Why token buckets?* Large requests allocate many tokens (sequence length x batch size) causing kernel queuing saturation. Per-priority token buckets limit how many tokens can be held by a single priority class without blocking others. *Why aging boost vs strict priority?* Strict priority can starvation-prone; aging boost retains fairness while letting low-latency work preempt long-running jobs after bounded waiting. *Why adaptive timeouts?* Bounding queue wait time ensures a predictable tail and allows the router to fallback to a different model/replica or to run a fast-path without batching when SLOs are at risk. Migration plan: roll out to perf-canary (20% traffic) for 48h, promote to canary (100% traffic to a subset of hosts) for 24h, then gradual fleet rollout. Observability: dashboards added under Observability > continuous-batcher > scheduler. Additional notes: kept existing public API unchanged; knobs are feature-flag guarded and default to previous behavior for stability.

release_notes: Improved continuous-batcher scheduler: better queue fairness, starvation prevention via aging boosts, per-priority token buckets, and bounded wait timeouts. Reduces p99 latency for latency-sensitive workloads under mixed traffic.
perf_summary: Canary perf (mixed small+large workload): low-latency class p50 ~ unchanged, p95 improved ~20ms, p99 improved from ~240ms to ~165ms. Overall batching efficiency within 3% of baseline. Starvation incidents dropped to 0 over 48h canary from ~7 prior incidents.
test_plan: Unit tests for weight/aging logic, integration test simulating mixed workloads, perf microbench, 48h perf-canary at 20% then 24h canary at subset hosts, rollouts gated on metrics thresholds defined in the PR checklist.
canary_result: perf-canary (20% traffic, 48h): pass, no regressions in throughput, p99 improvements observed. Full canary subset (24h): pass. Rollout to fleet started post-merge.
